Welcome. I’m so glad you’re here, ready to join me on a journey that’s both eye-opening and deeply important. Have you ever wondered how certain ideas—especially the ones about race—become woven into the very fabric of a nation?
Together, we’ll explore how racist beliefs didn’t just appear out of nowhere—they were built, debated, and carefully reinforced throughout American history. And as we go, we’ll see how these beliefs have shaped everything from laws and institutions to the way people interact every single day.
Drawing from Ibram X. Kendi’s powerful work, Stamped from the Beginning: The Definitive History of Racist Ideas in America, we’ll uncover the strategies and motivations behind these ideas—how they’ve been rationalized, disguised as progress, and used to justify inequality for generations.
We’ll meet some of the pivotal figures who influenced this narrative, see how their actions rippled across time, and discover just how adaptable—and persistent—racist ideas can be. It’s not just about the past; it’s about how culture, policy, and personal beliefs connect, and what that means for us now.
By digging into this history, we’re not just looking back—we’re preparing ourselves to face the present with greater clarity. If you’re ready to ask tough questions and open yourself to new insights, you’re in the right place.
Let’s get started—together, we’ll challenge old assumptions, spark new understanding, and imagine what a more just future could look like.
